summary.title: David A. Wheeler's Review of "Debugging" by David J. Agans
summary.one_liner: Learn the nine timeless rules of debugging from David J. Agans' book, as summarized and critiqued in David A. Wheeler's review.
keywords: change one thing at a time
if you didn't fix it it ain't fixed
how to find elusive software bugs
takeaways: Agans' book is built around nine debugging rules, each with sub-rules and illustrated by war stories.
Key rules include 'quit thinking and look' (gather data before guessing) and 'if you didn't fix it, it ain't fixed' (verify the fix).
The book focuses on timeless debugging principles rather than specific tools, so it complements tool-specific and testing books.
Intermittent-bug advice in the 'Make it Fail' rule is a standout, though the reviewer notes the book never names 'Heisenbug'.
Wheeler's critiques: no master list of sub-rules, and little detail on specific common debugging tools.
summary.summary: This is a review by David A. Wheeler of David J. Agans' book "Debugging: The 9 Indispensable Rules for Finding Even the Most Elusive Software and Hardware Problems." The review explains that the book covers fundamentals of locating and fixing bugs after detection, aimed mainly at novices and moderately experienced developers. It lists all nine rules with their sub-rules, and highlights the war stories used to illustrate them. Wheeler also compares the book with other debugging and testing titles and offers criticisms, such as the lack of a master list of sub-rules and limited tool-specific guidance.
